clue.text: Key book incorporated by degrees in film

explanation.surface: A film in which a key book was absorbed gradually, bit by bit.

clue.text: Sort of model to follow very quaint online post?

clue.text: English people occupied by old lady gas?

an old lady is a mother, so MA

explanation.definitionFit: A gas given off by something is an emission or exhalation, which is what this word means; the question mark flags it as an example.

clue.text: One's seen around swinging hotel chain

explanation.definitionFit: Ibis is a budget hotel brand run by Accor; it also names a wading bird, in keeping with the theme.

clue.text: Greyish-brown dope circulating Ohio prison

O is the abbreviation for the US state of Ohio

explanation.surface: Dull brown drugs passing round an Ohio jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground cell, a kind of prison, especially in a castle.

clue.text: Good period of time inhaling good grass?

an eon is a long period of time

clue.text: Shimmeringly coloured indiscreet shot

clue.text: Top dog to get a good score, of course

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of hound

clue.text: Idiot taking in Tyneside match on husband's birthday?

clue.text: Old king and a ploughman in conversation?

clue.text: Uplifting feeling provided by boundless sex

parts.note: sexual relations, or just relations, means sex

clue.text: Some partying Indians linking up?

clue.text: Colour film from Spielberg about a Liberal

parts.note: E.T. is Steven Spielberg's 1982 film

explanation.definitionFit: Teal is a dark blue-green shade, named after the duck's wing markings.

clue.text: Entire term ruined when one stops working?

indicators.note: ruined letters are broken up and rebuilt in another order

explanation.definitionFit: Leaving one's job for good, usually in old age, is called this; the question mark admits the phrase describes it rather than equals it.

clue.text: Singer client pays to change appearance

indicators.note: the letters alter how they look by being rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Patsy Cline was an American country singer, famous for 'Crazy'.

clue.text: Roman province train ban I affected

indicators.note: affected letters are altered, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: A Roman province hit by a rail ban I imposed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romans called their province covering most of Great Britain by this Latin name.

clue.text: US Air Force reconnaissance plane 22?

clue.text: One that will lift uncased grand into church

clue.text: Error with a sum annoyed suit-makers

indicators.note: annoyed letters are stirred up, so they are rearranged

clue.text: Topless outing with bit of sexual relations

clue.text: Court date city politician originally handed Sprite?

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

an MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: originally means taking the first letter

clue.text: Netted skunk, perhaps, outside B&B

parts.note: skunk is a strong strain of cannabis, an example of weed
bed and breakfast written as two Bs

indicators.note: the scrambled letters drink the port, taking it inside
done badly, the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

parts.note: a haven is a harbour

a score of nought by a batsman in cricket is called by this name

clue.text: Ken Loach film about sex toys
